questions.q: What happens by default when you save changes to an existing, previously saved flow?
options: The previous version is permanently overwritten
The flow is automatically deactivated
A new flow with a different API name is created
Flow Builder offers Save As, and 'A New Version' creates a new, separately numbered version without touching the old one
questions.explain: Saving as A New Version preserves every prior version intact in the flow's history instead of overwriting it.

questions.q: How many versions of a single flow can be active at the same time?
options: As many as you want
Two — one for testing, one for production
Exactly one — activating a version automatically deactivates whichever was active before
Zero; flows don't have an 'active' concept
questions.explain: Only one version of a flow can be active at any time; activating a new one deactivates the previously active version automatically.

questions.q: Where can you activate or deactivate a specific flow version without opening Flow Builder?
options: From the Flows list in Setup, using each flow's row-level dropdown
Only from within the Flow Builder canvas itself
Only through a Data Loader import
It's not possible outside of Apex code
questions.explain: Setup's Flows list lets you activate or deactivate a version directly from the list, without entering Flow Builder.

questions.q: A flow is on Version 4 (active), and you discover Version 3 worked correctly while Version 4 has a bug. What's the fastest fix?
options: Rebuild Version 3 from scratch using notes or memory
Contact Salesforce Support to restore a backup
Delete the flow and recreate it
Reactivate Version 3 from the Versions menu — it was never deleted
questions.explain: Because old versions stay intact and deactivated rather than disappearing, recovery is as simple as reactivating the last known-good version.

questions.q: Inside Flow Builder, where do you see the full list of a flow's saved versions and which one is currently active?
options: The Debug panel
The Toolbox panel on the left
The Versions menu, opened from the flow's name at the top of the canvas
The element's own context menu
questions.explain: The Versions menu, accessible from the flow name, lists every saved version with the active one clearly marked.
